interpretations: Rate is computed per media type as SUM(Bytes) / SUM(Milliseconds), the ratio of totals. The track count is COUNT(*) of tracks that join to a media type.
Rate is computed per media type as AVG(Bytes / Milliseconds), the mean of per-track ratios. The track count is COUNT(*) of tracks that join to a media type.
Rate is computed per media type as SUM(Bytes) / SUM(Milliseconds), but only over tracks with non-NULL Bytes. The track count is the number of tracks with non-NULL Bytes.
Rate is computed per media type as SUM(Bytes) / SUM(Milliseconds), but only over tracks with non-NULL Bytes. The track count is all tracks of that media type, including those with NULL Bytes.
"Matching media type" means an inner join between Track and MediaType, so tracks whose MediaTypeId has no MediaType row are excluded. Media types with no tracks are also excluded.
"Matching media type" means a left join from MediaType to Track, so media types with no tracks are included. Their rate is NULL or 0, and their track count is 0.
The "simple average of all media types' rates" is the unweighted mean of the per-type rates, with each type counted once. Types with a NULL rate are excluded from this mean.
The same simple average is taken over all media types, including those with zero tracks. Their rate is treated as 0.
The same simple average is taken over all media types, including those with zero tracks and a NULL rate. Averaging ignores the NULLs, which gives the same result as interpretation 7.
The average is computed over all media types in the MediaType table, while the displayed types are restricted to those with tracks.
"Above" means a strict comparison (rate > average). The alternative is rate >= average.
"How far the rate is above that average" is the absolute difference (rate − average).
"How far the rate is above that average" is the relative or percentage difference ((rate − average) / average, or ×100).
The rate is Bytes divided by Milliseconds, in bytes per millisecond.
The rate is Milliseconds divided by Bytes. This is the inverse reading and is unlikely.
Integer division is avoided by casting to a decimal or float, so the rate is a real number.
Integer division is used as the columns are stored, so the rate is truncated to a whole number.
"Don't round anything" means the full-precision values are returned with no ROUND function. The alternative is that the average and difference are also unrounded and the rate is not truncated.
The output columns are the media type name, rate, track count, and difference from the average, in that order.
The output includes the MediaTypeId as well as the name.
Media types sharing the same Name are grouped together by name rather than by MediaTypeId. The alternative is grouping by MediaTypeId, with duplicates shown separately.
Media types with a NULL Name are shown with a NULL name, or they are excluded.
Tracks with NULL Bytes are included, so Bytes is treated as 0 in the numerator, while their Milliseconds still counts in the denominator.
Tracks with NULL Bytes are excluded entirely, from both numerator and denominator.
Results are ordered by rate descending, by difference descending, by name, or not ordered at all.
Missing interpretations:
"How far the rate is above that average" is the ratio of the rate to the average (rate / average), not a difference.
Rate is AVG(Bytes / Milliseconds) over per-track ratios, with tracks that have NULL Bytes excluded from both the rate and the track count.
Rate is AVG(Bytes / Milliseconds) over per-track ratios, with NULL-Bytes tracks ignored in the rate but still counted in the track count.
Tracks with Milliseconds = 0 are excluded to avoid division by zero, in either the per-track ratio or the ratio of totals.
The simple average is computed only over media types that pass the filter (non-NULL rate and at least one track), and the "above average" comparison and the difference both use that same value.
queries:
SELECT m.Name, SUM(t.Bytes) * 1.0 / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS Rate, COUNT(*) AS TrackCount
FROM Track t
JOIN MediaType m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name

SELECT m.Name, COUNT(*) AS TrackCount, AVG(t.Bytes * 1.0 / t.Milliseconds) AS Rate
FROM Track t
JOIN MediaType m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name;

SELECT m.Name, CAST(SUM(t.Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS Rate, COUNT(*) AS TrackCount
FROM Track t
JOIN MediaType m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
WHERE t.Bytes IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name;

SELECT m.Name, COUNT(*) AS track_count, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN t.Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN t.Bytes END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN t.Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN t.Milliseconds END) AS rate
FROM MediaType m
JOIN Track t ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name
